51339446.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His-tagged recombinant human HDAC8 by SPR assay
51339446.original_paragraph: SPR experiments were performed at room temperature using the Biacore T200 (GE Healthcare) and a dextran-coated gold sensor chip functionalized with nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) (Series S Sensor Chip NTA, GE Healthcare). Recombinant human his-tagged HDAC8 (R&D systems) was immobilized using Ni2+-NTA affinity and then stabilized via amine coupling using N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) and 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC). Measurements were performed in pH 7.4 phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) running buffer, including 0.05% Tween 20, 3mM EDTA, and 1% DMSO. HDAC8 immobilization and surface preparation was performed in pH 7.4 PBS, including 0.05% Tween 20. The surfaces of flow cells two (Fc2) and one (Fc1) were conditioned with 350 mM EDTA (GE Healthcare) for 60 seconds at a flow rate of 30 µL·min-1. Fc2 was then prepared for ligand immobilization with 0.5 mM NiCl (GE Healthcare) injection at 30 µL·min-1. The surface of Fc(2) was then activated with 420sec injection of solution containing 0.5M NHS and 2M EDC (GE Healthcare) at a flow rate of 10 µL·min-1. His-tagged HDAC8 (6ug/ml, pH 7.4 PBS) was injected onto to FC2 and 10 µL· min-1 until at least 4000 RU was reached, and the surface was inactivated with 420 second injection of pH 8.0 1M Ethanolamine-HCl (GE Healthcare) at a flow rate of 10 µL· min-1. Fc1 was prepared in a similar manner without NiCl and his-tagged HDAC8 injections. Single cycle kinetics was used to collect kinetic data. Compounds diluted in running buffer were injected over the two flow cells over 5 different concentrations at a flow rate of 50 µL· min-1 and a contact time of 60 seconds. The complex was allowed to dissociate for 420 seconds. The surfaces were regenerated with two 10 seconds injections of 9:1 1M NaCl: Glycerol at a flow rate of 30 µL· min-1. Data was double referenced by subtracting binding responses from running buffer injections flown over the active (Fc2) and reference (Fc1) flow cell. Data were collected at a rate of 10 Hz and fitted to a 1:1 kinetic model using the global data analysis option available within BiaEvaluation 3.0 software.
